title: The Coin Flip That Explained the Whole FTX Case, According to the Judge
hook: The coin flip|the judge read out.

lines.say: At Sam Bankman-Fried's sentencing, Judge Lewis Kaplan read aloud from Caroline Ellison's trial testimony.
She said he talked about taking a coin flip where tails might lose ten million dollars, and heads might make slightly more.
lines.show: She said he talked about taking a coin flip where tails might lose $10 million, and heads might make slightly more.

lines.say: And that he would be happy to flip a coin where tails meant the world was destroyed, as long as heads made the world more than twice as good.

scene.q: … he would be happy to flip a coin if it came up tails and the world was destroyed. As long as if it came up heads, the world would be like more than twice as good.

lines.say: The judge called it a leitmotif of the entire case.

scene.q: that's really a leitmotif in my judgment of this entire case.

lines.say: FTX customer funds, he said, were not his to use. He was betting on expected value.
Real trials. Real evidence. The verdict.
